pr_title: drivers: sensor: stm32_temp: Fix + add support for STM32G0B1
pr_body: Remove unnecessary calibration, fix for `stm32_temp`, add support for STM32G0B1 STM32G0B1 datasheet: I think the configurations should be similar across G0 family, but the TS_CAL2 seems to be missing from other series (at least G0B0 & G070), so I decided to leave them out from this PR for now. pr_comments:
@erwango I wonder what would happen if there are multiple threads/work that use the same ADC? All of them will setup the channel and then do `adc_read`. What happens if an interrupt occurs after the 1st thread setup the channel, and after servicing that interrupt, the scheduler schedules the other thread to run which setup & read the ADC in one go. Finally the 1st thread is scheduled and resume to continue from `adc_read`, but this time it would be reading the wrong channel configuration? @andyross Is what I described here possible?

Do you think we need a mutex lock in the `adc_channel_setup` & unlock at the end of `adc_read`, so that we can guarantee that the same thread will setup and read the ADC before another thread uses the ADC? The downside is that a thread will probably have to always setup the ADC before read, even if it is the only user of the entire application.

> @erwango I wonder what would happen if there are multiple threads/work that use the same ADC? All of them will setup the channel and then do `adc_read`. What happens if an interrupt occurs after the 1st thread setup the channel, and after servicing that interrupt, the scheduler schedules the other thread to run which setup & read the ADC in one go. Finally the 1st thread is scheduled and resume to continue from `adc_read`, but this time it would be reading the wrong channel configuration? @andyross Is what I described here possible?
> 
> Do you think we need a mutex lock in the `adc_channel_setup` & unlock at the end of `adc_read`, so that we can guarantee that the same thread will setup and read the ADC before another thread uses the ADC? The downside is that a thread will probably have to always setup the ADC before read, even if it is the only user of the entire application.

Could you explain why you need to re-setup the channel every sample read? It's not clear to me in the description why this change is made. Since channel setup is done every sample read, it will also re-calibrate the adc every time. This looks like a bit overdoing it?

When I was testing the die temp sensor (on a STM32L5), the temperature was also a bit higher than the ambient temp, but I think this is because it's a bit heating during runtime. It's a die temperature sensor afterall. At cold startup, the temp of the die is about the ambient temp if I recall correctly. 
(Nevertheless, very jealous about your ambient temp :-) )

> Could you explain why you need to re-setup the channel every sample read? It's not clear to me in the description why this change is made. Since channel setup is done every sample read, it will also re-calibrate the adc every time. This looks like a bit overdoing it?

What if you have another thread that is using the ADC to sample another channel, when that thread configure the ADC, wouldn't it overwrite the configuration done by `stm32_temp`?

> it will also re-calibrate the adc every time

I have removed the calibration flag, so the `stm32_temp` will not calibrate the ADC anymore. The ADC calibration is done when the ADC driver inits.

> Nevertheless, very jealous about your ambient temp :-)

It's an air-conditioned room, otherwise it would be 38 degree in the afternoon ☹️

comments: @ycsin G0 temp sensor probably requires this https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/41295

I think the first part of the problem (acquisition time) is due to this [line](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/adc/adc_stm32.c#L789), where all channels need to have the same acquisition time on G0 series.

The second part (calibration) might be a bug in the adc driver which is fixed recently by bc1b262885c3e91b3391a10dc7ecf8b489065998
